name: physics
title: Physics
summary: Open quantum systems, quantum circuits with a simulator, finite elements (FEniCS and scikit-fem) and finite volumes for PDEs, molecular dynamics with LAMMPS, curve fitting and units.

tools.name: qutip
tools.does: open quantum systems: states, operators, master equations, time evolution
tools.check: python -c "import qutip as q; print('ev', round(float(q.expect(q.sigmaz(), q.basis(2,0))),1))"

tools.name: qiskit
tools.does: quantum circuits, with the Aer simulator to run them (no real hardware: runs have no network)
tools.usage: python: from qiskit import QuantumCircuit; from qiskit_aer import AerSimulator
tools.check: python -c "from qiskit import QuantumCircuit; from qiskit_aer import AerSimulator; c=QuantumCircuit(2); c.h(0); c.cx(0,1); c.measure_all(); r=AerSimulator(seed_simulator=1).run(c,shots=200).result().get_counts(); print('bell', sorted(r)==['00','11'])"

tools.name: scikit-fem
tools.does: finite elements in pure Python: assemble and solve PDEs on triangular, quadrilateral and tetrahedral meshes
tools.check: python -c "from skfem import *; from skfem.models.poisson import laplace, unit_load; m=MeshTri().refined(4); b=Basis(m,ElementTriP1()); x=solve(*condense(asm(laplace,b),asm(unit_load,b),D=b.get_dofs())); print('max', round(float(x.max()),2))"

tools.name: fipy
tools.does: finite-volume PDE solver: diffusion, convection, phase field

tools.name: lammps
tools.does: classical molecular dynamics for particles, materials and soft matter
tools.check:
printf 'units lj
lattice fcc 0.8442
region b block 0 3 0 3 0 3
create_box 1 b
create_atoms 1 box
mass 1 1.0
pair_style lj/cut 2.5
pair_coeff 1 1 1.0 1.0
run 0
' > t.in; lmp -in t.in -log none | grep -c 'Created 108 atoms'

tools.name: lmfit, pint, uncertainties
tools.does: curve fitting with parameter bounds and uncertainties (lmfit); physical units (pint); error propagation (uncertainties)
tools.check: python -c "import lmfit, uncertainties, pint; u=pint.UnitRegistry(); print((3*u.m/u.s).to(u.km/u.hour))"

tools.name: fenics
tools.does: the FEniCS finite-element system (DOLFINx 0.5): PDEs written as variational forms and solved on meshes. It runs under its own Python: start scripts with fenics-python, not python. The first use of a form compiles it, which takes some seconds
tools.usage: fenics-python script.py   (import dolfinx, ufl; from mpi4py import MPI)
tools.check: fenics-python -c "from mpi4py import MPI; from dolfinx import mesh, fem; m=mesh.create_unit_square(MPI.COMM_WORLD,8,8); V=fem.FunctionSpace(m,('Lagrange',1)); print('dofs', V.dofmap.index_map.size_global)" 2>&1 | tail -2
